clue.text: Doctor in study, a genius

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: a den is a private study or retreat
MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A brilliant doctor spending time in their study.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor goes into the study between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exceptionally skilled is called a demon at it, and a genius was originally a guardian spirit, as a daemon is.

clue.text: Show abbreviation for European Parliament in concise dictionary

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: a concise, shortened form of the word dictionary
the initials of European Parliament

explanation.surface: An instruction to display how a dictionary abbreviates the European Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concise' tells you to shorten dictionary to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to portray or represent it, a verb synonym of show.

clue.text: Just yours truly on bank

blocks.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Someone simply sitting on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' sits between the pieces as a link: bank on means rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely and just are adverb synonyms meaning only, nothing more than.

clue.text: General waiting to give compulsory army training?

blocks.note: general in the sense of nationwide, as in a general election
waiting at table is service

explanation.surface: An army general hanging about before running a training course for conscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: General looks like a military rank, fitting the army picture, but it is an adjective meaning countrywide. Britain had this conscription until 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: National service was a period of obligatory military duty for young men, an example of enforced soldiering instruction.

clue.text: Finished among a group left behind

indicators.note: something placed among a group is set inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group of people or musicians
finished means done

explanation.surface: Someone who is finished in a band ends up left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The finishing word goes inside the group word, between its N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been deserted, left behind by those who had it.

clue.text: Master at sea heading for Doha, a medium-sized port

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
the first letter of Doha
taken as written
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A ship's master sailing towards Doha from a mid-sized harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Master at sea fits a ship's captain perfectly, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is a Dutch city and a major harbour, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Expect a delay

blocks.note: taken as written
a wait is a delay

explanation.surface: Bracing yourself for a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to see the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to look forward to it as coming, a verb synonym of expect.

clue.text: Determined to examine the result of a move on board

definitions.text: the result of a move on board

blocks.note: determined in the sense of found out, ascertained
to check is to examine

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to inspect what happened after a chess move.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, a discovered check happens when moving one piece uncovers an attack on the king by another. Determined looks like resolute, but means found out.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess term names a check on the king revealed when a different piece moves out of the line of attack.

clue.text: Two nouns covering love and understanding? Drivel

indicators.note: the outer pieces cover what sits between them, wrapping round it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for noun, twice
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
sense is understanding or good judgment

explanation.surface: A grammatical claim that two nouns can capture love and understanding, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ns go either side of the O, then the understanding word follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense and drivel are noun synonyms for silly, meaningless talk.

clue.text: Reduction in iron?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fall in the amount of the metal iron, as in a diet or ore
setter's reading: what a clothes iron does is take out folds from fabric, a de-creasing

explanation.walkthrough: Iron reads as the metal, but think of the household appliance: ironing removes creases, so split the answer as de-crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a lessening or drop, a noun synonym of reduction.

clue.text: Copyright infringers, Irish, filling tapes criminally

indicators.note: doing something criminally means bending the rules, so the letters are twisted out of order
something filling another goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled round the inserted letters
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Irish bootleggers illegally copying cassette tapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the tapes, then put the Irish abbreviation after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are people who illegally copy and sell protected works such as recordings or software.

clue.text: As is nacre, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A comparison: something is like mother-of-pearl, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a conjunction starting the sentence; it is the chemical symbol, the definition. Nacre is mother-of-pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the poisonous element arsenic in the periodic table.

clue.text: Most inexperienced , OK, in new sect

indicators.note: a new version of something is a remade one, so the letters are rearranged
one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
to OK something is to allow it

explanation.surface: The greenest recruits are welcome in a newly founded religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: OK here is a verb, to approve; the rearranged sect wraps around it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means young and lacking experience, so its superlative means the greenest of all.

clue.text: Honours cheque, ultimately (indecently large)

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour; plural here
the last letter of cheque

explanation.surface: A payment for honours, with a parenthetical sneer at its size.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an award given in the UK honours lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, an adjective meaning excessively fat or large in body.

clue.text: Proverb striking one SAS operative - see, mood's changing

indicators.note: something changing alters its form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: striking in looks means handsome
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written: the Special Air Service regiment
a hand is a worker or operative, as in factory hand
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A handsome SAS soldier whose mood keeps shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: SAS operative reads as one soldier, but SAS stands alone and operative is a worker. The proverb means good conduct counts more than good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known saying, so the answer is an example of a traditional maxim.

clue.text: Method of selection, unusual on isle abroad

blocks.note: odd means unusual
the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland
out and abroad both mean out of doors, about

explanation.surface: An odd way of choosing who goes to some foreign island.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd man out is also a way of picking one person by tossing coins until one differs from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd man out is a coin-tossing game that singles out one player, a way of choosing.

clue.text: Dictionary in judge's room

blocks.note: first meaning: a well-known dictionary much loved by crossword setters
second meaning: the private office where a judge works

explanation.surface: A dictionary sitting in a judge's private office.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a British dictionary publisher; a judge hears matters privately in chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a published lexicon and the private office of a judge or barrister.

clue.text: Curse song about a capital in Africa

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
the capital of a word is its initial upper-case letter

blocks.note: an anthem is a song of praise or loyalty
taken as written
the first letter of Africa

explanation.surface: A song cursing some African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital in Africa looks like a city such as Nairobi; it means only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical ban or curse, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: See 13
Connected with game, racket

blocks.note: a tie is a match or game, as in a cup tie
a racket is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: A tennis match linked to a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket suggests a tennis racket alongside the game; here it is noise. A cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied in, as in tied in with, means linked or associated with something.

clue.text: Engineers' former tax break

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
cess is an old word for a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tax break that engineers used to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tax break reads as one phrase, but break is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or interval, as a school or parliamentary recess, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Travel by car from Palermo to Rome

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the end of Palermo, all of to, and the start of Rome

explanation.surface: Driving the road from Palermo up to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to drive or go somewhere in an automobile, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Concession made by Fischer, an eccentric

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A concession won from Bobby Fischer, the famously eccentric chess champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence or right granted to trade, a kind of concession.

clue.text: Norse goddess Jeffrey Archer includes

indicators.note: the name includes the letters within it, sitting inside the phrase

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of Jeffrey and the start of Archer

explanation.surface: The novelist Jeffrey Archer puts a Norse goddess in one of his books.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse deity of love and fertility in Scandinavian mythology.

clue.text: Hermit showing up before child

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A recluse emerging ahead of a child.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious recluse, an old word for one who lives alone apart from society.

clue.text: Late extra anticipated

blocks.note: over means extra, left over
something due is expected

explanation.surface: Something extra arrived later than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means behind schedule, an adjective synonym of late.

clue.text: Type of surgery not required by member

blocks.note: spare means surplus, not needed
a part is a member of a whole

explanation.surface: An operation an organ or limb does not actually need.
explanation.walkthrough: Member suggests a limb, fitting the surgery picture, but it simply means a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare-part surgery is an informal term for transplanting organs or fitting artificial ones.

clue.text: Two-part book from Henry James, or Edward Lear?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Old Testament books in two parts, First and Second
second meaning: Henry, James, Edward and Lear are all names of monarchs

explanation.walkthrough: Henry James and Edward Lear look like two writers; split them into four royal names. Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a two-volume Bible book and also monarchs, which every one of those four names belongs to.
